name: Timeline Analysis
description: Ability to construct and analyse forensic timelines (super-timelines) from multiple evidence sources. Covers extracting timestamps from filesystem metadata, log files, registry entries, browser history, and application artifacts, then correlating them to reconstruct sequences of events.

0.label: None
0.description: No exposure to forensic timeline analysis

1.label: Awareness
1.description: Understands the concept of forensic timelines and why correlating timestamps matters in investigations
evidence: Can explain what a super-timeline is and its role in forensic investigations
Understands MACB timestamps and their forensic meaning (e.g. NTFS $STANDARD_INFORMATION vs. $FILE_NAME attributes)
Can describe common timestamp sources (filesystem, registry, logs, browser)

2.label: Guided Practice
2.description: Generates and filters timelines using established tools under supervision
evidence: Generated super-timelines using log2timeline/plaso under guidance
Filtered and searched timeline data using Timeline Explorer or similar tools
Identified key events in a timeline exercise with supervisor assistance
Documented timeline findings with proper timestamp format and timezone notation

3.label: Independent Practice
3.description: Independently constructs comprehensive timelines and uses them to answer investigative questions
evidence: Built and analysed super-timelines in 5+ real investigations
Correctly resolved timezone discrepancies across multiple evidence sources
Used timeline analysis to establish user activity sequences in case reports
Timeline-based findings accepted in case reports without significant revision

4.label: Advanced / Mentor
4.description: Handles complex multi-source timelines; detects timestamp manipulation; correlates timelines across multiple systems
evidence: Correlated timelines across multiple systems and evidence sources in a single investigation
Detected timestamp manipulation and anti-forensic timeline artifacts
Developed custom plaso parsers or timeline processing scripts for novel artifact types
Mentors junior examiners on timeline construction and interpretation

5.label: Expert / Authority
5.description: Defines timeline analysis methodology; researches timestamp artifact behaviour; provides expert testimony on event reconstruction
evidence: Authored or maintains the lab's timeline analysis methodology
Published research on timestamp artifact behaviour or timeline analysis techniques
Provides expert testimony on event reconstruction based on timeline evidence
Trains teams on advanced timeline analysis and correlation techniques

assessment_methods.description: Given a multi-source disk image, generate a super-timeline, resolve timezone issues, and produce a chronological narrative of key events
Presented with conflicting timestamps across evidence sources, determine the correct sequence of events and explain discrepancies
